analysis.title: Longevity weekly pulse #82: Conference takeaways
key_insights: Longevity is both a demographic challenge and a cross-sector opportunity spanning health care, consumer, travel, automation and wealth management. Demographic change is gradual, giving governments, businesses and markets time to adapt.

Panelists said raising birth rates is unlikely to solve pension and economic pressures. Improving health care, education, economic security and productivity matters more, with the focus on staying healthier for longer.

A growing and wealthier older population is creating demand for premium travel, experiences, luxury and lifestyle products. Intergenerational wealth transfer and the growing financial influence of women are changing spending patterns.
AI, robotics and automation can offset labor shortages and some economic pressure from an aging workforce through productivity gains.
Roche's CFO said 2027 starts a significant launch cycle, with about 20 new molecular entities expected by 2030 across oncology, neuroscience and immunology.
Roche management believes outer-year consensus sales for giredestrant are too conservative and expects a strong acceleration after launch.
Fenebrutinib has potential peak sales of about CHF 3bn, with a differentiated efficacy profile in relapsing and primary progressive MS. Liver toxicity remains a consideration.

Roche expects strong sales growth and improving margins in 2027 despite higher pipeline investment. It has about CHF 20bn in free cash flow but stays disciplined on valuations and targets. UBS views Roche's loss-of-exclusivity pressure as more manageable than peers'.
Novartis management reiterated guidance of a 5-6% sales CAGR over 2025-30. Kisqali has potential peak sales of USD 10bn, and Kesimpta and Leqvio continue to perform well.

Rhapsido is progressing after its US launch, with management targeting about USD 4bn in peak sales across dermatology and immunology. Management sees potential for it to become Novartis' largest drug ever.

Novartis patent expiries are Cosentyx in 2029 and Kesimpta/Kisqali in 2031. Management believes the next generation of growth drivers can more than offset them, backed by about USD 13bn of annual R&D.

Novartis reiterated its ambition of a 40% operating margin by 2029. Capital allocation priorities are unchanged: dividend growth, buybacks of about USD 1.2-1.3bn (mainly offsetting dilution), R&D and bolt-on M&A.
Rhapsido has attractive economics: low cost of goods and limited incremental sales and marketing spend, given Novartis' existing MS commercial infrastructure.

From 1 November 2026 UBS CIO no longer rates or ranks equities as Most Preferred or Least Preferred. It uses a 'CIO Selected' designation instead, which is not a rating. Most Longevity list names are shown as CIO Selected or were previously Most Preferred.

market_movers.rationale: UBS CIO remains positive on Roche and calls it a core holding in its Longevity list, citing the 2027 launch cycle and margin outlook.
UBS believes Novartis can sustain growth beyond the patent expiry cycle on Kisqali, Rhapsido and R&D investment. Pipeline execution is the key risk.

sector_views.rationale: Prevention, cardiovascular health, obesity management and mental health are highlighted as longevity beneficiaries, and Roche and Novartis launch cycles are supportive.
A wealthier, longer-living older population is driving demand for premium travel, experiences and lifestyle products.

earnings_insights: Novartis guidance: 5-6% sales CAGR over 2025-30, as stated by management. This is guidance, not a reported result.
Novartis targets a 40% operating margin by 2029 (management ambition, not a reported figure).
Roche expects strong sales growth and improving margins in 2027 (management outlook). It has around CHF 20bn in free cash flow.
risk_factors: Roche-specific: lower Vabysmo penetration against the Eylea 8mg launch, Ocrevus competition from Kesimpta and BTK inhibitors, and new entrants in HER2.

Novartis-specific: weaker commercial success of key assets, generic erosion for Entresto and other drugs losing exclusivity, Cosentyx price/volume competition, reduced cardiovascular launch expectations and missing medium-term margin targets.
Fenebrutinib liver toxicity remains a consideration.
Failure of pipeline execution would undermine Novartis' ability to replace expiring patents.
